posts.title: Hanging Out
posts.excerpt: The importance of casual communal experience.
posts.body:
I have always longed to be carefree and I am in love and hate everyone who is. If you too aren't one of the care free, you probably recognize this feeling, if you are, I don't know what to say to you. I grew up afraid of the world and my way of coping was to be extremely careful. Caring developed into my mode of creativity which is centrally about caring for things, caring what this next to that is or might become, caring why I do this or that and not this other thing. The artist cares, even if at times their care turns into a fire that burns down entire villages. 

So what about Hanging Out? My interest in exploring the topic of Hanging Out is that it seems to be a place of carefree togetherness in which there can be a free flow of experimentation of selves. There is no goal in Hanging Out, except a kind of opting out from goals. In college this is a time of not-doing, of procrastinating on the work that has been assigned. And yet I am convinced that Hanging Out is likely a crucial aspect of a liberal arts education, which is to say, of learning how to be the best form of oneself in a society. 

More on this another time...
